/Issued 111 PM MDT Sun Sep 13 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

An upper level low positioned over eastern WA this afternoon 
shifts east across the Northern Rockies overnight, emerging along 
the AB/MT border Monday morning then continues east through 
Monday afternoon. Enhanced mid-level flow ahead of the trough and 
afternoon heating/mixing continues is promoting the downward 
transport of gusty south/southwest winds across portions of SW MT 
with sustained south winds in excess of 30 mph and a few gusts 
over 50 mph focused along the Madison River Valley, where terrain 
aligns with the mid-level flow and a High Wind Warning is in 
effect until 6 PM. Showers and a few thunderstorms develop ahead 
of the incoming upper level low late this afternoon with coverage 
increasing across central/north-central MT this evening. Gusty 
winds across SW MT will diminish early this evening as mixing 
decreases and an inverted surface trough and cold front begin to 
shift across the region. Gusty west winds, cooler temperatures and
decreasing showers sweep east across the rest of central and 
north-central MT overnight behind the passage of these features. 
Another round of showers circulates around the mid-upper low as it
emerges east of the Rockies Monday morning, mainly focused along 
the continental divide with a few showers tracking east across 
central and north-central MT through Monday afternoon as the upper
level low tracks east. Snow levels still look to fall to around 
6500 ft overnight across the Glacier NP and Rocky Mtn Front region
and eventually across the rest of north-central and SW MT by 
Monday morning. 

Northwest flow behind the departing upper low and a strong surface
pressure gradient thanks to low pressure deepening across ND will
support gusty winds across much of north-central MT on Monday with
strongest winds across eastern portions of central MT Monday afternoon.
Broad mid-level troughing and a lingering cool surface airmass
will remain situated over MT through Tuesday prior to flow shifting
south-southwesterly mid to late week as a weaker upper low lifts 
northeast out of the CA/Great Basin region. Temperatures return to
near or slightly above normal values Wednesday through the weekend.
Model guidance displays some variance regarding the timing and extent
of moisture with the Great Basin feature; however, this system will
bring warmer air alongside shower and potential thunderstorm activity,
primarily impacting SW MT late Thursday into Friday before potentially
spreading northward across central and north-central MT over the 
weekend.

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Although mid-level lapse rates in excess of 8C/km are present late
this afternoon, the strength of convection through this evening may
be somewhat constrained by CAPE values generally remaining below 
500 J/kg. Nevertheless, mid-level wind speeds and shear increasing
to 50 kt will sustain a threat for gusty winds and possibly even 
some small hail in stronger cells. High-resolution model ensembles
target the Great Falls to Havre corridor for the highest concentration
of showers and thunderstorms between 6 pm and 9pm, with weaker 
activity shifting east across JB, Fergus and Blaine counties by 
midnight. 

Snow showers later tonight through Monday morning will primarily 
affect the higher peaks along the continental divide north of MT-200
with up to 1 inch of snow accumulation possible at Logan Pass in 
Glacier NP. Additional showers circulating across the central MT 
mountains Monday morning could see some enhancement across the 
Little Belts with a period of snow showers bringing some minor 
accumulation to the Kings Hill area as well. 

High Wind Watches remain in effect for portions of Judith Basin and
Fergus counties on Monday, where there is a broad 50-70% probability
of gusts in excess of 55 mph with a 60-80% probability primarily 
across southeast portions of Fergus county. Hoenisch
